title: Manager, Product Management (Sustainability and Financial Inclusion)
description:
**Our Purpose**

*Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.*

**Title and Summary**

Manager, Product Management (Sustainability and Financial Inclusion)Overview:
  
  
At Mastercard, we are focused on building an inclusive, sustainable digital economy, where everyone has an opportunity to reach their potential. We see firsthand how our commitment to environmental and social responsibility - and our core value of operating ethically and responsibly and with decency - is directly connected to our continuing success as a business. We recognize that Mastercard cannot succeed in a failing world. We thrive when economies thrive, and a successful economy is sustainable only when it is inclusive and when prosperity is shared.  
  
We are building a sustainable world that unlocks priceless possibilities for all by focusing on the following key areas of impact:
  
  
Environmental Stewardship: Responsibly managing our environmental footprint and creating environmentally conscious solutions  
  
Inclusive Growth: Creating a more inclusive world through our products, programs, and partnerships  
  
Our People and Culture: Leveraging our core values to make our company the place where the best people choose to be  
  
Ethical and Responsible Standards: Acting responsibly and with integrity guided by the highest standards of ethical behavior  
  
The Role:
  
  

* As a Manager for Sustainability and Financial Inclusion, you will join the Sustainability team and be responsible for reinforcing our sustainability and business strategy. This role will be based in Singapore.

  

* The successful candidate will be responsible for planning and coordinating Mastercard’s product/commercial Sustainability activities for the Asia Pacific region. The role requires the individual to possess a strong combination of strategic, commercial, project and product management mindset. You will handle product integration/deployment and have a thorough understanding of product details for new as well as existing products & services.

  

* You will play an active role in launching and monitoring product/program performance, scaling and driving adoption, as it relates to Sustainability and Financial Inclusion initiatives relating to Priceless Planet Coalition, Carbon Calculator and connecting 500 million people and small businesses to digital pathways that promote long-term resilience across AP. As part of these initiatives, you will collaborate and coordinate across Divisions/Markets, Region and Global.

  

* You will help shape and advance Mastercard’s regional sustainability and financial inclusion agenda by driving strategic insights, impact measurement, and performance visibility across key initiatives. This includes supporting the tracking and articulation of outcomes related to financial inclusion and financial health priorities, alongside sustainability programs such as Priceless Planet Coalition and the Mastercard Carbon Calculator.

  

* Working closely with cross functional teams, market stakeholders, and external partners, you will help translate data, market intelligence, and program outcomes into meaningful business and impact narratives that support strategic decision making, regional priorities, stakeholder engagement, and long-term growth objectives.

  

* The role requires you to have a continual look at the market & track competition, to see how our products can be improved to meet the evolving needs of the end-consumers & to bench mark our products with that of competition.

  
  
All About You:
  
  

* Strong knowledge of, and interest in, sustainability, financial inclusion, financial health, or related fields, with the ability to understand emerging market trends, stakeholder priorities, and the evolving business landscape shaping these agendas.

  

* Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to develop executive-ready briefings, presentations, and strategic recommendations for senior stakeholders.

  

* Able to navigate, influence, and lead cross functional collaboration across diverse stakeholders and functions, with comfort operating in ambiguous and fast evolving environments while delivering clear outcomes.

  

* Proven project management and execution capabilities, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously, drive coordination across internal and external stakeholders, and deliver against key timelines and priorities.

  

* Competent in leading product solutioning and technical discussions with internal and external stakeholders, with experience supporting the launch and scaling of products or services across one or multiple markets.

  

* Exceptional analytical and commercial acumen, with the ability to build robust business cases that clearly articulate the incremental value and impact of our solutions for customers and Mastercard.

  

* Ability to conduct financial and cost-benefit analyses to support strategic decision making, product enhancements, and internal investment approvals.

**Corporate Security Responsibility**

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:

* Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;
* Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
* Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
* Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

**About the Orange Movement**

Launched in 2022, the Orange Movement™ is a global initiative led by IIX Global to integrate gender equality and climate action into financial markets. At its core are Orange Bonds™ — the world's first gender-lens and climate-focused asset class — designed to.

* Mobilize US$15 billion in capital markets by 2030
* Positively impact 150 million women, girls, and gender minorities
* Position women and gender minorities as leaders in climate resilience and adaptation

The Orange Movement advances this vision through capital mobilization, policy reform, global partnerships, training, and advocacy. With US$2 billion already mobilized and a new US$1 billion Orange Climate Fund anchoring a US$10 billion cooperation agreement with the Government of Indonesia, the Movement is entering a pivotal scale-up phase — with an active co-funder base, formalized governance infrastructure, and the Orange Forum as its flagship annual convening. IIX seeks a Senior Director who can build the Movement into an institution with the financial strength, governance maturity, and operating capability to stand on its own for the long term

**Role Summary**

The Senior Director of the Orange Movement will provide strategic vision, entrepreneurial drive, and organizational leadership to build the Movement into a durable, self-sustaining institution — expanding its reach, resources, and financial independence globally. This is a rare opportunity to take a coalition at the intersection of finance, gender, and climate from an IIX-incubated initiative to a mature institution with genuine systems-change potential.

**This senior leadership role will:**

* Own and manage the Orange Movement program, working closely with IIX teams — including Sustainable Finance and the newly established Impact & ESG Advisory — as they execute Orange transactions and related projects.
* Ensure the long-term financial sustainability of the Orange Movement through diversified, multi-year fundraising — spanning co-funders, grants, and catalytic capital.
* Mature the coalition's governance infrastructure into a standard-setting model for stakeholder management, built to operate independently over time.
* Spearhead co-funder cultivation, partnership pipeline development, and multi-year fundraising.

This position is ideal for a leader who combines deep networks across finance, philanthropy, and development with the entrepreneurial instincts to build lasting institutions — equally comfortable setting strategy and doing the hands-on work of standing up the operating backbone a growing coalition needs.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Partnerships & Global Alliances**

* Develop and execute a global strategy to expand the Orange Investor Alliance and Partner Coalition
* Build and own a structured co-funder pipeline — from identification and cultivation through to close and stewardship
* Engage institutional investors, DFIs, corporates, philanthropies, and governments as strategic allies and co-funders of the Orange Movement's mission
* Build trust with policymakers, regulators, and multilaterals to embed Orange standards into financial systems
* Use CRM systems and research tools to maintain a living, high-quality partnerships database
* Engage the newly established Impact & ESG Advisory as a technical thought partner on measurement, standards, and reporting for Orange instruments

**Fundraising & Financial Sustainability**

* Own and drive the Orange Movement's co-funder and fundraising strategy — from identification and cultivation through to closing institutional partnerships with foundations, DFIs, and impact investors
* Mobilize grants and catalytic capital to scale the Movement, targeting US$2M+ in co-funder contributions in Year 1 and scaling year over year, securing multi-year funding commitments alongside IIX senior management
* Build the Orange Movement's long-term financial sustainability model — including piloting fee-based membership and certification revenue streams — steadily reducing the Movement's reliance on IIX's core platform over time
* Maintain best-in-class fundraising collateral, funder value propositions, and a structured partnerships pipeline across the co-funder lifecycle

**Training & Market Building**

* Lead the Orange Capital Verifier Training program and similar certification tracks
* Expand training offerings for investors, regulators, and issuers to build global confidence in Orange instruments — including blended/digital learning formats
* Partner with universities, think tanks, and global institutions to mainstream Orange finance education
* Own the roadmap for establishing the Orange Capital Principles, Orange Seal, and Orange Index as recognized, market-wide reference standards for gender-lens and climate-aligned finance

**Coalition Governance & Institutional Development**

* Serve as Secretariat for the Steering Committee, Advisory Council, and Working Groups — driving formalisation, documentation, and distributed knowledge management
* Build and own a structured onboarding process for incoming coalition members
* Ensure inclusive, accountable, and transparent governance — supported by clear meeting cadences, action tracking, and member engagement protocols
* Diagnose and address engagement gaps across working groups, including reviving or restructuring underperforming groups as needed
* Evolve the coalition's governance bodies — Steering Committee, Advisory Council, Working Groups — into a mature structure capable of governing the Movement independently at scale

**Advocacy, Convenings & Thought Leadership**

* Lead the flagship Orange Forum and other global convenings, owning the partnerships and stakeholder coordination layer
* Curate high-impact campaigns that place Orange Financing at the center of global finance dialogues
* Publish research, thought leadership, and storytelling that amplify Orange's influence

**WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR**

**Experience & Skills**

* Bachelor's degree required; MBA or Master's in Business, Finance, Public Policy, or International Development preferred
* 15+ years in strategic partnerships, capital markets, fundraising, or senior leadership roles in finance, philanthropy, or development — with meaningful experience in the Global South
* Proven track record in capital mobilization, impact finance, or climate/gender initiatives
* Demonstrated ability to build and lead cross-functional teams, work across global stakeholders, and operate entrepreneurially in frontier markets
* An existing, activatable network of funder relationships — DFIs, foundations, corporates, multilaterals — capable of converting into signed co-funder commitments within the first 12 months
* Experience with CRM systems (Salesforce, Airtable, HubSpot) and digital collaboration platforms; familiarity with AI productivity tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Notion AI, etc.)
* Exceptional fundraising, partnership-building, and strategic execution skills

**The Person**

* Visionary and entrepreneurial — able to push system-level change while operating in ambiguous, fast-moving environments
* Resilient, with the credibility and presence to build trust across DFIs, governments, UN agencies, and Fortune 500s
* Equally comfortable setting strategy and doing the hands-on work of standing up the operating backbone a growing coalition needs

**THE PREM FRAMEWORK**

Every IIX team member is a PREM professional. We look for these qualities in everyone we hire:

**P- Passionate**

Mission-driven & purpose-led

**R - Resilient**

Thrives under pressure & ambiguity

**E - Equitable**

Champions fairness & inclusion

**M - Maverick**

Bold, entrepreneurial thinker

**WHY IIX**

* Lead a global movement advancing gender equality and climate action — with a mandate to build it into a lasting, independent institution.
* Build a legacy platform targeting 100 million lives by 2030.
* Operate at the nexus of finance, development, and advocacy.
* Work with world-leading institutions — from DFIs and governments to UN agencies and Fortune 500s.

**At IIX, we seek individuals who are:**

* Passionate — committed to gender equality and climate action.
* Resilient — able to navigate challenges in frontier markets.
* Equitable — dedicated to measurable social and financial outcomes.
* Entrepreneurial — bold, innovative, and able to build something new.

Job Title: Research Fellow (Environmental Economics)

University-Level Unit: College of Design and Engineering

Faculty/Department-Level Unit: Civil and Environmental Engineering

Employee Category: Research Staff

Location\\_ONB: Kent Ridge Campus

Posting Start Date: 24/07/2026

**Job Description**
-------------------

The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at the National University of Singapore (NUS) invites applications for a Research Fellow to join an interdisciplinary research project on the development of an AI-driven climate–air quality coupling model for practical applications. The project aims to integrate climate science, air quality modelling, artificial intelligence, and environmental economics to generate policy-relevant insights for sustainable development and climate change mitigation.

  

The successful candidate is required to work closely with a multidisciplinary team of researchers to evaluate the socioeconomic drivers and policy impacts associated with future air quality under alternative climate and development scenarios.

**Job Requirements**
--------------------

* Possess a PhD in Environmental Economics, Resource Economics, Applied Economics, or a closely related discipline.
* Demonstrated expertise in environmental economics, climate policy, or sustainability economics.
* Strong knowledge and practical experience in Difference-in-Differences (DID) models and other causal inference methods.
* Experience working with large socioeconomic, environmental, or policy datasets.
* Strong quantitative and econometric skills.
* Proficiency in statistical software such as R, Stata, Python, or MATLAB.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* A strong publication records commensurate with career stage.
* Open to fixed-term contract.
